relevance_note: A dystonia exome cohort paper with one family carrying compound heterozygous ALDH5A1 variants: "Only one family (DYS-71) with ALDH5A1 biallelic pathogenic variants was found to have T2 hyperintensity in BG".
method_note: Read by hand; a short script only assembled the JSON. Only family DYS-71 (Table 2, two ALDH5A1 rows, zygosity CH) is in scope; all other families have variants in other genes and get no rows. The paper reports ALDH5A1 findings at family level only and never says how many affected members DYS-71 has; I recorded one person, 'unnamed person 1' with family label DYS-71, standing for the affected member(s); no sex, age, or individual label is given. Cohort size: 42 families with 46 affected and 47 non-affected individuals; 46 recorded as cohort_size_as_stated. Disease label comes from Table 2's 'Disease involvement' column, which the table note says is OMIM-based information on the gene's disease involvement, not necessarily a clinical diagnosis. Dystonia is recorded as observed from the group statement that all 42 study families are dystonia families (inferred from group statement). 'T2 hyperintensity in BG' (basal ganglia) is recorded as a feature but the checklist item 'T2 hyperintensity of globus pallidus, subthalamic or dentate nuclei on MRI' is left not reported, because BG is broader than the named nuclei. Table 1 'additional clinical characteristics' are counts without names and exclude no one. The metabolic finding reads 'Decreased urine 4-hydroxybutyric acid (0 mmol/mol)' for both ALDH5A1 rows; recorded as printed. Variant type not stated per variant (the text's 'two stop-gain, two frameshift and one splicing variants' refers to the established dystonia genes), so not reported. No parental testing result stated for DYS-71; inheritance not reported. cites_prior_report is true because three families were published previously, but the paper does not say DYS-71 is one of them. Supplementary excerpts contain no DYS-71 patient-level ALDH5A1 data. No contradictions found.
